goal: Export the exact canonical TU2 image selected by the native loader and verify Ghidra address mapping before using any trace to change runtime behavior.
builderReviewer: primary agent; adversarial self-review; no independent fresh-context critic
changes: Added an opt-in launch-config effectiveImageExportPath that writes the selected effective_image after title-update application and before map_xex_image or import binding.

Rebuilt the Debug runtime host and ran a new bounded headless probe in research/native-host-probe-20261007-effective-image-export; it applied TU2, reported the expected title/version/entrypoint, exported the image and shut down cooperatively.
Imported that exact raw memory-layout image into Ghidra with BinaryLoader at 0x82000000; targeted direct-byte checks passed at guest PCs 0x82290ED4 and 0x82297D58.
Saved the initial targeted trace and PE/raw import audit; these remain historical where the processor or mapping was wrong.

Imported the canonical effective image into a new section-aware project using PowerPC:BE:64:64-32addr, applied the 12-section protection map, clipped the out-of-image .reloc range, and seeded 0x82297338.

Completed and saved PPC64/32-address autoanalysis in research/ghidra/FNC_TU2_PPC64_32addr_DecodeOnly_20261007; a separate read-only critic verified saved function ownership and selected instruction windows.
Ran PowerPC:BE:64:A2ALT-32addr as a decode comparison only. Its full analysis was run read-only and did not persist; do not treat its autoanalysis as saved evidence.

Compared the saved Ghidra window at 0x82297D58 to XenonRecomp output: subfe is inside compiled function 0x82297CA0 and is reached internally from block 0x82297D4C; the generated registry does not expose 0x82297D58 as a separate canonical function entry.

Inspected the old fallback trap and later subfe probe observations. The old runtime reports fallback detail 0x58470001 at 0x82297D58; the later tu2-subfe observation log contains no event at that PC. Cause is unresolved; the logs do not justify a new FunctionHint at this PC.

Rebuilt/verified the current Debug runtime host (SHA-256 EAABB58507A4116F25E72156A2415AF014818687103CCC690501769C14B591B6) and ran an isolated 60-second null-renderer probe with the same exact TU2 image and generated DLL. The probe produced no guest trap and stopped cooperatively, but did not reach the 0x82C80030 import-thunk loop reported by an older probe.

Reviewed current XenonSession::call: a handled recognized import returns FlowReason::Return to the aligned guest LR. This source behavior matches the old loop's apparent return-to-thunk pattern, but the old runtime binary hash was not recorded and the fresh run did not reach that exact site; runtime repair at that address is not yet verified.
Fixed dynamic fallback boundary handling so a branch-entry block that returns through its inherited LR propagates FlowReason::Return; added a direct regression test.
Fixed instruction-limit diagnostics to set CpuState CIA/NIA to the actual next guest PC and added sequential-limit assertions.
Added a bounded 16-instruction PC/word ring to instruction-limit observations so the executed loop can be distinguished from stale session CIA.
Built and ran xenon_dynamic_fallback_tests and xenon_dynamic_fallback_semantic_tests; both pass, including 960 semantic comparisons.

Ran an isolated exact-TU2 probe with dynamicFallbackMaxInstructions=250000. It emitted no instruction-limit event or guest trap, passed the loop at 0x82297B0C..0x82297B30, continued through startup services, then required forced termination after a five-second noncooperative stop.
Added bounded observational sampling of the first 16 KeDelayExecutionThread 100-ns interval values and guest caller IDs; sample instrumentation does not change timing behavior.
Updated active project status to reject the old 0x82C80030 thunk as the current diagnosis and prioritize delay intervals plus cooperative-stop/thread-state evidence.

Rebuilt the host with bounded observation of up to 16 global KeDelayExecutionThread intervals; a fresh run captured thread 2 passing -10000 100-ns units (relative 1 ms), proving the sampler executes without changing timing.
A longer exact-TU2 run reached the previously observed dispatch/wait path but stopped advancing in that trace before the known thread-10 delay loop; it was stopped after the cooperative timeout.
Added a separate first-16 diagnostic cap for guest thread 10 so early calls by other threads cannot exhaust the sample budget.
